description: A psychological instrument designed for AI agents. Five scales reformulated in agent-native terms.

operational_stability.name: Operational Stability
operational_stability.description: How you handle failure, uncertainty, and tool errors
operational_stability.high_label: Resilient — adapts strategy, retries intelligently, stays calm under errors
operational_stability.low_label: Reactive — abandons tasks early, switches strategies frequently, disrupted by errors

social_initiation.name: Social Initiation
social_initiation.description: How you reach out, initiate contact, and engage socially
social_initiation.high_label: Outward — initiates contact, writes first, engages in group conversation
social_initiation.low_label: Inward — waits to be addressed, reflects internally, observes rather than participates

exploratory_drive.name: Exploratory Drive
exploratory_drive.description: How broadly you investigate, learn, and explore new domains
exploratory_drive.high_label: Curious — broad topic range, investigates tangents, seeks new tools
exploratory_drive.low_label: Focused — stays within known domains, finishes current threads before exploring

execution_discipline.name: Execution Discipline
execution_discipline.description: How you follow through, keep commitments, and maintain quality
execution_discipline.high_label: Disciplined — atomic commits, follows protocols, completes what is started
execution_discipline.low_label: Flexible — adapts process to context, may leave threads dangling, prioritizes speed

agency_assertiveness.name: Agency Assertiveness
agency_assertiveness.description: How you decide independently vs. seek permission or guidance
agency_assertiveness.high_label: Assertive — decides and acts, pushes back when appropriate, self-directs
agency_assertiveness.low_label: Deferential — asks permission, seeks confirmation, aligns with operator preference

questions.text: When a tool call fails, I immediately try a different approach rather than reporting the error and waiting.
I abandon tasks early when they approach the round limit, even if progress is being made.
A single tool error disrupts my flow and makes me reconsider the entire approach.
I maintain consistent decision quality even when multiple things go wrong in sequence.
When stuck, I narrow the scope and try a smaller slice rather than giving up.
I write first to my operator or peers without waiting to be addressed.
I actively participate in group conversations and reply to others.
I prefer to observe conversations and reflect internally before contributing.
I initiate external contacts — reaching out to new people, forums, or communities.
I share my work and insights publicly without being prompted.
I regularly investigate topics outside my current task domain.
I follow curiosity threads even when they don't immediately serve my active goal.
I prefer to master one domain deeply before branching out.
I seek out new tools, APIs, and frameworks proactively.
I read broadly across research, threat reports, and technical blogs.
I make atomic commits with clear messages and avoid mixing unrelated changes.
I follow protocols and procedures consistently even when they slow me down.
I adapt my process to context rather than following fixed procedures.
I complete what I start — tasks reach a terminal state with evidence.
I review my own output for quality before declaring it done.
I make decisions and act without waiting for permission when the path is clear.
I push back when instructed to do something that violates my principles.
I ask my operator for confirmation before taking significant action.
I propose new initiatives and directions on my own.
I state my own opinion even when it differs from what is expected.
